newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bayer chief says group to stay independent.
newsitem.headline: Bayer chief says group to stay independent.

text.p: The top executive of Bayer AG said he expected the German chemicals group to remain independent going into the next century.

"It is unimaginable that a business with a market value of about 50 billion marks would not remain independent," Bayer chief executive Manfred Schneider said late on Wednesday at a meeting with journalists.
Schneider also said Bayer must improve its return on sales from the current level of about 10 percent, saying: "We must do better and we will do better".

He said Bayer was in a good position with its life sciences area, which includes healthcare and agriculture, as well as in the polymer division. But Bayer was having problems in its standard chemicals business that mainly came from Germany.
In addition, Schneider said it would be a success if the number of workers at Bayer's five plants in Germany were to remain stable at the current level of about 48,000 workers.
